CausalChain: Tumor cells produce EVs loaded with miR-155 and other modulators -> EVs are internalized by mature neutrophils -> EV cargo activates mTOR signaling in neutrophils -> mTOR activation drives metabolic reprogramming -> Neutrophils differentiate into granulocytic-MDSCs -> Granulocytic-MDSCs suppress T-cell activity and promote tumor progression
Hypothesis: Inhibition of mTOR signaling in mature neutrophils during tumor-derived EV uptake will prevent their conversion into immunosuppressive granulocytic-MDSCs, thereby reducing tumor immune evasion and improving responses to immunotherapy.
Abstract: Our study proposes a novel mechanism by which tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) reprogram mature neutrophils into immunosuppressive granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) via activation of mTOR signaling. EVs released by tumor cells, enriched in modulatory factors such as miR-155, may trigger metabolic reprogramming in neutrophils, transforming them from active immune effector cells into cells that potently suppress T-cell responses and foster an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Blocking mTOR activation during EV uptake could inhibit this phenotypic conversion, thereby mitigating immune evasion and enhancing the therapeutic efficacy of cancer immunotherapies.
